reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Forehead involved means lower motor neuron lesion
Bell palsy: steroids within 72 hours plus eye care
Transverse temporal fracture: SNHL plus facial palsy
House Brackmann grades I normal to VI total
reference.pathophysiology: Viral inflammation swells the nerve inside its narrowest bony segment compressing its blood supply; fracture fragments or haematoma injure directly, while regenerating axons misdirect to wrong muscles and glands.
additionalDifferentials: Central forehead sparing versus peripheral palsy
Otogenic palsy versus idiopathic Bell palsy
additionalInvestigations: House Brackmann grading and eye examination
MRI when atypical, slow or recurrent; audiometry
